records.implementation: Every finding's evaluation record carries automatable (VER-EVA-AIA): yes by default; no only from a decision record carrying the evidence (decisions.schema.json 'automatable', and _decisions.py refuses 'no' without evidence) or a CVSS 4.0 AU:N. Figure 7's floor reads the vector as the automatable proxy, and a finding with no prediction score is LEV, as the method states; an EPSS score below the governed threshold (published with its rationale, REQ-LEV-2) is the method's evidence for NLEV.

Each finding carries an evaluation record with every factor VER-EVA-EFA names, each with its basis: criticality (the component's classification, which PAIN is computed from), reachability (IRV and basis), exploitability (LEV and basis), detectability (outside-in, public advisory, public source), prevalence (findings and components in its group, share of the inventory), privilege (CVSS PR/S and identity or key components), proximate vulnerabilities (other findings and verified mitigations on the component, read with the group) and known threats (KEV, EPSS). The VDR methodology publishes what each factor means (methodology.evaluation_factors). The factors are recorded, not fed into the global impact tables (REQ-PAI-4); grouping feeds the policy.

False-positive is a governed disposition: decision records with justification, decided_by/on, review_by (data/decisions.json: 13 false-positive records, e.g. DEC-039 ZAP 10099 'pattern matched prose', DEC-040 'Server: AmazonS3 carries no version'); triage.rego:262 record_status rejects a false positive that names a control (it must be 'mitigated') and lapses at review_by; live report: 30 findings with final_disposition false-positive, each with a decision_id.

policies/triage.rego decides IRV from an outside-in observation, the resolved inventory component's declared internet_reachable, or a verified not-reachable mitigation, with irv_basis per finding. Suppressions resolve to the resources their decision names, a site-root DAST finding resolves to its page, and a finding that still resolves to no component is rated at the method's fail-safe (IRV) and recorded as vdr.unresolved-component, a process finding with a deadline until it resolves.

Figure 7 in policies/triage.rego, first match deciding, with lev_basis per finding. Configuration checks carry no CVE, so each recurring check has a governed CVSS vector (infrastructure/schemas/check-vectors.json) adopted by decision record DEC-180; a decided vector whose record is not in force stops the build. The vector drives the floor and the no-direct-impact rule, so LEV reflects what exploiting the misconfiguration needs in this system; DAST findings are evaluated by their decision records (DEC-039, DEC-040); anything unevaluated keeps the default (LEV).

PAIN is computed by the CVSS-Environmental derivation from the vector (the advisory's, or the governed check vector adopted by DEC-180) and the component's classification, onto the rules' scale; a fully mitigated finding takes N0, read from VER-EVA-EPA in the rules. Each finding states its likely agency effect and what the rating rests on (impact_rationale), which the VDT carries as potentialAgencyImpact.
